subtitle: Master the architectural principles of songwriting through music theory analysis

overview.title: Understanding Song Architecture
overview.text: Song structure is the blueprint that guides listeners through a musical journey. Rather than memorizing patterns, we'll explore why certain structures work by understanding the underlying harmonic, melodic, and rhythmic principles.

columns.title: Functional Analysis
columns.text: Learn to identify the harmonic function of each section and how it serves the song's emotional arc.

columns.title: Tension & Release
columns.text: Understand how sections create and resolve musical tension through chord progressions and melody.

topics.title: Verse
topics.description: The narrative foundation - learn how verses develop melodically and harmonically to tell the story.

topics.title: Chorus
topics.description: The emotional peak - understand how choruses use harmonic tension and melodic climax for impact.

topics.title: Bridge
topics.description: The contrast section - explore how bridges provide harmonic and melodic departure from main themes.

topics.title: Intro
topics.description: Setting the stage - analyze how intros establish key, mood, and musical themes for the song.

topics.title: Outro
topics.description: The resolution - study different ending techniques and how they provide harmonic closure.

topics.title: Pre-Chorus
topics.description: Building tension - learn how pre-choruses create harmonic and rhythmic momentum toward the chorus.

topics.title: Song Forms
topics.description: Common structures - understand AABA, verse-chorus, and other traditional song forms and their theory.

topics.title: Transitions
topics.description: Connecting sections - master the harmonic and rhythmic techniques that smoothly link song parts.

columns.title: "Sweet Child O'Mine" Structure Analysis
columns.text:
Intro: Iconic riff in D major establishes harmonic center
Verse: D-C-G progression creates stable foundation
Chorus: Returns to D major with added harmonic movement

Bridge: Modulates to create contrast and build tension
Solo: Extended harmonic exploration over familiar progression
Outro: Gradual fade maintains energy while providing closure
